the proposed management model enables the automatic adaptation of a service-level to client requirements, in the presence of network sub-system changes or failures.

the development of a generic management framework that can be used to manage the quality of service of any network application.
the management of network services in a manner that enables their adaptation to changes in the underlying network resources.
the design and development of generic service-level management modules, which can be reused across a range of distributed adaptive applications.

this paper presents a novel approach towards service management of distributed network applications, and the approach is generic and independent of the specifics in problem domain.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our approach enables a client application to specify its requirements in a generic manner, and the management module to automatically monitor and reconfigure the network infrastructure to meet the requirements.
the paper proposes a model of service-level management for distributed network applications that are adaptive to changes in the underlying network resources.
the proposed management model enables a network administrator to configure the network resources to provide services to clients, and the clients to configure the services to meet their needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a management module, independent of the specifics in the underlying network infrastructure, can be developed to enable the automatic reconfiguration of a client-level service in response to resource-level changes in the underlying network.
service-level management can be made independent of the problem domain, and can be realized through a generic model of service provisioning.

the service-level management of distributed applications should not be application-specific, but should instead be a generic service that may be reused across applications, thereby reducing the cost and effort of developing adaptive applications.
